title: Cost Sprint Guild: Roadmap + Health Thermometer for Prefetch/Batch/Quant
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Initiative to coordinate a cross-functional "frugal serving" sprint that targets 3 levers (batching, prefix/KV prefetch caching, and quantization profiles). Deliverables are: 1) a two-week experiment roadmap that produces validated, rollout-ready configs; 2) a lightweight "health thermometer" metric set for go/no-go decisions; and 3) a rollout checklist and auto-rollback policy for the Console. This ticket tracks progress, decisions, and blockers for the guild that includes PM, Eng infra, Runtime, and Design.
updates: 2025-02-10: Kickoff meeting. Agreed on scope: focus first on high-volume conversational routes and embeddings batch jobs. Owners: Luca (PM lead), Priya Shah (Runtime), Jordan Kim (Infra), Noor Patel (Design).

2025-02-12: Defined health thermometer metrics: cost_delta_per_1k_tokens (%), p95_latency_change_ms, quality_regression_rate_pp (human eval harness), rollout_coverage (% of traffic), incident_rate_change (incidents/week). Metric thresholds for canary: cost savings >= 8% AND p95_latency_change <= +20ms AND quality_regression_rate <= 0.5pp. Documented in confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/frugal-sprint/thermometer (PRD v0.1).

2025-02-14: Experiment matrix drafted: 9 arms (3 batching configs x 3 quant profiles) x 2 cache TTLs. Prioritized by estimated savings and risk. See experiment tracker sheet: https://docs.redwood.ai/sheets/frugal-experiments. Estimate: 72 total runs across dev/dev-1/dedicated staging.

2025-02-18: Runtime team prototype of adaptive batcher showed 6–10% token-cost improvement in synthetic trace; p95 latency increased 12ms in worst-case. Flag: the current kernel selection logic doesn't favor low-batch tails and needs a heuristic tweak (ENG-1842).

2025-02-21: Design reviewed rollback UX for Console canary toggles; suggested adding explicit 'quality regression guardrail' state with recommended next steps. PRD updated with wireframes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FrugalConsoleUX

2025-02-24: QA harness integration: introduced small human eval set (n=250 prompts) for fidelity checks post-quant. Early runs show 0.6pp regression for the most aggressive quant profile — exceeds threshold. Decided to de-prioritize that profile for canary. Action: Runtime to produce intermediate quant step.

2025-02-28: Canary plan approved for batching+moderate-quant+cache-TTL-6m. Canary rollout policy: start 0.5% traffic, monitor 4h windows, expand to 5% if therm. green, expand to 25% after 24h, full rollout at 72h. Auto-rollback triggers: quality_regression_rate > 0.5pp OR incident_rate_change > 2x baseline OR p95_latency_change > +50ms. Documented in rollout-checklist.md (GitHub Gist): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-gists/rollout-checklist

2025-03-02: Stakeholder review (eng + legal). Legal flagged telemetry retention for prefetch keys; agreed to pseudonymize keys and restrict retention to 30 days (security_review_required=false but follow-up compliance task created).

2025-03-04: First staging canary run completed. Observed: cost_delta_per_1k_tokens = 9.2%, p95_latency_change = +14ms, quality_regression_rate = 0.2pp, no incidents. Passed canary gate. Notes: cache pressure on small GPU instances higher than expected; infra recommends soft prefetch backpressure when memory > 75% (ENG-2219 follow-up).

2025-03-05: Decision log update: proceed to prod canary with conservative expansion windows. Next steps: (1) coordinate with SRE for rollout windows (Luca + Jordan), (2) schedule customer-impact review for customers on Dedicated (Priya), (3) add detailed per-route telemetry to Console dashboard (Design + Console eng).
open_blockers: Kernel selection heuristic causes p99 spikes at low-batch tails; pending patch in runtime (ENG-1842).
Automated human-eval pipeline needs scale to 1k prompts for robust signal; infra quota request submitted.
Quant toolchain currently lacks intermediate 4-bit profile; runtime to add medium-risk profile before next canary.
acceptance_criteria: Validated experiment results showing >=8% token-cost savings at production traffic for at least two high-volume routes without violating temperature thresholds for quality and latency.
Health thermometer automated in Console with clear green/yellow/red states and links to drilldowns for failed checks.
Rollout checklist and auto-rollback policies implemented and smoke-tested in staging; SRE runbook updated.
next_steps: Schedule prod-canary window with SRE and narrow blast radius (owner: Luca) — target 2025-03-07 morning window.
Runtime: land kernel heuristic patch and add medium-risk quant profile (owner: Priya) — target 2025-03-06.
Console: implement health thermometer panel and per-route telemetry drilldowns (owner: Noor) — target 2025-03-10.
PM: prepare customer communication plan for Dedicated customers affected by early rollouts (owner: Luca) — target 2025-03-08.
